shots.description: Fade in on abyssal black lamp room. The dead lamp is a black monolith; the only light is the jar on the floorboards, a faint ember-blue coal. Lightning rims the gallery glass, sketching Espen small and mid-frame. Blacks never crush — jar glow keeps every surface just legible.

Minute one. Boy hands jam a rag and his balled jacket into the cracked storm-green pane; the wind bulges the cloth back at him twice, fighting him for it. Knuckles white in jar-blue and lightning rim; no warm light anywhere yet.

Medium: he crosses to the great lens, jar-glow throwing his shadow tall across brass and glass. The six-note litany figure enters — one note, low, like a bell underwater. Composition tilts the lamp huge, the boy small.

Minute two. Fingers on the wick scissors, trembling but working. Slow push toward the trim: blue light on brass, breath fogging in the cold. The motions are hers — we can feel the drill under the panic.

Minute three, tight inserts: oil to the ring. His shaking fingers land in exact registration with Orla's from scene 5 — knuckle for knuckle, same framing, intercut so his hands and the memory of hers become one pair. Ember dusk of the memory flickers against the abyssal blue of now.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Minute three. Oil to the ring.

shots.description: Minute four. The tin, filling frame. First match drawn across the striker — the head crumbles wet against it, a sound like sand. The orange flare never comes; only damp grit falling. The tin he pocketed undried is lying, because he made it lie.
Second match. Third. Both crumble; wet head-paste on his fingertips. His hands start to hurry — the exact opposite of the drill. The litany note under this one lands flat, degrading.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: No. No no no. Not now—

shots.description: Seven small deaths. He shelters the tin inside his shirt; four, five, six, seven die in close-up — each dud laid gently on the white sill in a lengthening row, filmed like casualties. We count the row, never his face. Litany figure keeps losing pitch as each match goes.
His eye, huge, rimmed in jar-blue; a held single close-up. He steadies his voice with her words — the drill as a handrail.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Minute five. Strike away from your body.

shots.description: The eighth match snaps unstruck between his fingers — two clean pieces on his palm. He is bargaining with a clock now. Sting under the snap; the litany dies with it.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: That was still five. It's still five!

shots.description: The world changes. The jar on the floor wakes — ember-blue floods up to drowned-noon-blue, brightening until the whole room reads underwater. Push in until the glow fills frame.

Wide on the gallery glass: the rain stops falling DOWN and streams SIDEWAYS across the panes like current — physics of weather replaced by physics of water. Espen tiny against the glass wall, lit drowned-noon-blue from the floor.

Tilt up the black spiral stair as a long hull-creak rolls up through the tower from ten fathoms of stone below; dust sifts from the joints. Jar-blue spill bleeding down from the lamp room above keeps the dark readable.

Outside the gallery glass: rows of faint cold fin-lights rise past, huge and slow, orderly as lanterns in a procession — the Dry Sea filling with darkness that moves like deep water. Their light is the frame's only source; the tower glass reflects them in cold rows.
the vast undertow shape slides past the gallery glass, close, fills frame, fin-lights raking the dark, no eye visible, frost blooming across the pane, lighthouse unlit

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: You're not real. The sea left.

shots.description: Cold-open reprise one, wider and heavier: the sea coming back wrong — darkness sliding over the moonlit flats like a tide with no water in it, keeling the ship skeletons upright again. Slow pull back; silence holds.
Reprise two: the dark leaning at a lone dead lamp — Saltwick Light a black tooth against fin-light rows, the darkness pressed against the lamp-room glass like surf against a hull.
Reprise three: emptiness where a beam should be. The sky over the strait holds no line of light at all — just the risen dark and a thin lightning rim on the cloudwall.
her hand slack on the wet stone beside the still-swaying rope, six steps down on the landing; the bell barely ticks
Pressure valve two: the village's lit windows floating in the risen dark like buoys on a black swell — and going out one by one as people sleep, not knowing the tide is under them.

He stops looking at the eye and looks at the lens. Espen's silhouette turns from the frost-bloomed glass to the great dark lens, drowned-noon-blue behind him. The decision happens in posture, not face.

He remembers her HANDS, not her words: flash-insert of scene 5 — the wrist-grip, her salt-cracked fingers guiding his to the brass clip behind the lens. The score returns as a single sustained tone, one held note. Ember-dusk memory light against the blue.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: Behind the lens. One spare. Dry.

shots.description: The brass clip behind the great lens, found by feel: one match, dry as a kept promise. Push in as his fingers close around it — the smallest object in the episode carrying the most weight.

He shields the match inside her hanging coat — the wool a tent against the draft — and strikes it away from his body on the lens frame, exactly as taught. Match-flare orange: the first warm light of the scene, blooming inside the coat like a heart.

subs.speaker: ESPEN
subs.text: For the night the tin lies.

shots.description: The flame walks trembling to the wick. At the count of six, on the word, the wick catches — orange takes the frame from the blue in one breath.

The beam slams outward through the gallery glass and the darkness recoils from it like surf off rock — fin-light rows scattering, the sideways rain snapping back into ordinary falling weather. Pull back with the beam as it claims the air.

Wide and final: dry land restored under the sweeping beam, the flats bone-pale again where the light passes. One whale-deep note sinks below the cliff and does not come back. Hold, then fade to black on the turning beam.
